title: Setting the active cap at first run
story: As the owner, I want Ritmo to ask how many projects I can touch in a bad week, so that the cap comes from my real capacity instead of a number someone picked.
criteria: First setup asks for the bad-week number and uses the answer as the cap.
No constant cap is shipped in the product.
The question names a bad week explicitly, not an average one.

title: Choosing what is active, without softening
story: As the owner, I want to be made to choose only what fits the cap and shelve the rest, so that I stop carrying eight half-finished things.
criteria: Everything beyond the cap is shelved, and the count is shown plainly.
Shelved items stay visible in the portfolio with their why-this-is-mine.
No copy softens, congratulates or apologises for the number.

title: Opening on Monday
story: As the owner, I want the week to open showing what moved rather than what is outstanding, so that opening Ritmo is not an accounting of failure.
criteria: The landing surface renders recent progress before any backlog.
Nothing from the previous week is carried as debt.
Monday is the only point at which the active set can change, and changing it costs nothing.

title: Logging on a twenty-minute day
story: As the owner with twenty minutes between a deploy and dinner, I want the next action already written so that I spend the time working rather than deciding.
criteria: Each active project shows exactly one next action, written as trigger and act.
A progress entry can be saved in under 20 seconds from opening the app.
Effort and note are optional on the entry.

title: Work in the fixed job that also teaches me something
story: As the owner, I want an entry logged against a fixed-job project to also credit a learning objective in another area, so that one action advances two things.
criteria: An entry can name one additional objective from a different area.
The objective's derived state counts that entry as a touch.
Fixed-job projects never consume a slot from the active cap.

title: Spending a reserve instead of failing
story: As the owner whose week broke, I want to spend a declared reserve so that the commitment stays intact and I come back next week.
criteria: Every recurring commitment carries a reserve of ceil(0.30 x target), minimum 1.
Spending a reserve is recorded as an event with an optional note.
The commitment is not marked failed while reserve remains, and no penalty language appears.

title: The week that went to nothing
story: As the owner who lost a week to leisure rather than to an emergency, I want to name what took it in one tap and see the pattern over time, without any hours being counted.
criteria: The close accepts one optional tag from tags the owner defines.
No duration is recorded for anything outside a project, and no gap between available and logged hours is computed.
The pattern is shown across roughly eight weeks, only in the close, never in red and never accumulated as debt.
A week closed without a tag is as complete as one with it.

title: Closing the week
story: As the owner, I want to label how the week actually went after it happened and write a short reflection, so that the next proposal fits my real capacity.
criteria: The capacity label is applied retroactively at close and is optional.
No flow asks the owner to describe a bad day while having one.
A week closed without a label still trains the proposal from inference alone.
The next week's proposal derives from logged history and is editable.

title: An objective that has gone quiet
story: As the owner, I want an objective with nothing live under it to read as dormant rather than as failing, so that pausing a trip or a visa is a decision instead of a defeat.
criteria: An objective with no active project for four weeks reads as dormant.
Shelve and revive are both offered, in neutral language.
No percentage of progress toward the objective is shown, and no date is invented for it.

title: Advancing something I am still learning
story: As the owner learning three.js, I want progress measured by strategies tried and evidence gathered rather than by units delivered, so that a failed attempt still counts.
criteria: An objective can be typed as learning or as outcome.
A learning objective is scored on entries describing attempts, including unsuccessful ones.
A learning objective still requires a project beneath it, or it goes dormant.

title: A date I did not choose
story: As the owner building a site for my sister's wedding, I want the real date to order priority and protect the project's slot without Ritmo scheduling my hours.
criteria: A hard date can be set only when marked as externally imposed.
The date affects ordering and slot protection only.
No hour, block or reminder is generated from it.
